newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO opens Akzo bookbuilding.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO opens Akzo bookbuilding.

text.p: ABN AMRO Rothschild said on Thursday it had started the bookbuilding procedure for the sale of up to 6.6 million ordinary shares in Dutch Chemicals group Akzo Nobel.

Akzo said earlier it had agreed to waive a two-year standstill agreement on the sale of a 10.2 percent stake in the company held by Sweden's Securum AB in the interests of a controlled placement with long-term institutional investors.
A syndicate had been formed and the bookbuilding was expected to end on March 6, with allocations to be made the following day, ABN AMRO said.
In addition, investment firm Arnhemsche Maatschappij tot het houden van aandelen Akzo Nobel would issue between 7 and 15 million new shares, excluding a 15 percent greenshoe, the bank said.
Its subscription period starts tomorrow and will end on March 13. Arnhemsche will use the proceeds to acquire ordinary shares in Akzo Nobel, the bank said.
Arnhemsche will acquire one Akzo Nobel share for every ten it issues, it said, meaning it will get between 700,000 and 1.5 million Akzo ordinary shares.

The Arnhemsche shares will have an offer price of one tenth of the closing price of Akzo ordinary shares on the closing day of the subscription, plus a bookbuilding increment of between two and three percent.

The combined transaction amounts to the 10.2 percent shareholding of Securum in Akzo Nobel, ABN AMRO said, but does not include the 3 percent on which Securum sold two-year call options in April 1996. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
